q: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and ____.
e: The environment is the surroundings comprising of hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere and biosphere. Biosphere is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for a long period in the atmosphere, on land, in water or beneath the Earth's ____.
e: In the natural matter cycling, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulphur take a variety of chemical forms and may exist for a long period in the atmosphere, on land, in water or beneath the Earth's surface. Surface is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms and their locations in the biosphere are called a ____ cycle.
e: The pathways that allow different chemical substances to move through living and non-living forms and their locations in the biosphere are called a biogeochemical cycle. A biogeochemical cycle moves an element through rocks, water, air, and living things.

q: The cycling of elements is interconnected with the water ____.
e: The cycling of elements is interconnected with the water cycle. Cycle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and ____.
e: Most of the Earth's carbon is stored in rocks and sediments. Sediments is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The processes involved in the carbon cycle are photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and ____.
e: The processes involved in the carbon cycle are photosynthesis, respiration, exchange, fossilisation, sedimentation, and combustion. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Plants constantly exchange carbon with the atmosphere by absorbing carbon dioxide during ____.
e: Plants constantly exchange carbon with the atmosphere by absorbing carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living ____.
e: Respiration is the process of gas exchange between the atmosphere and living organisms. Organisms is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the fossilisation process, the animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and ____.
e: In the fossilisation process, the animal and plant residues become sediment and eventually turn into rock and minerals. Minerals is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The nitrogen cycle involves the following steps: nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and ____.
e: The nitrogen cycle involves the following steps: nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen assimilation, ammonification, and denitrification. Denitrification is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Unlike many other cycling elements, phosphorus cannot be found in the ____.
e: Unlike many other cycling elements, phosphorus cannot be found in the air. Air is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions $PO_4^{3-}$ and ____.
e: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for plants and animals in the form of ions PO43- and HPO42-. HPO42- is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphorus is also a building block of certain parts of the human including DNA and animal bodies, such as bones and ____.
e: Phosphorus is also a building block of certain parts of the human including DNA and animal bodies, such as bones and teeth. Teeth is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the soil, phosphorus occurs as rock phosphate, calcium phosphate, iron phosphate, or aluminium ____.
e: In the soil, phosphorus occurs as rock phosphate, calcium phosphate, iron phosphate, or aluminium phosphate. Phosphate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Phosphate salts that are released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by ____.
e: Phosphate salts that are released from rocks through weathering dissolve in water present in soil and will be absorbed by plants. Plants is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Marine birds play a unique role in the phosphorus cycle, as they take phosphorus-containing fish out of the ocean and return to land, where they ____.
e: Marine birds play a unique role in the phosphorus cycle, as they take phosphorus-containing fish out of the ocean and return to land, where they defecate. The phosphorus cycle moves phosphorus through rocks, water, and living things, with no long-lived gas phase.

q: Their ____ contains a high level of phosphorus and in this way, marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land.
e: Their guano contains a high level of phosphorus and in this way, marine birds return phosphorus from the ocean to the land. Guano is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The sulphur cycle moves through the rocks, water bodies, atmosphere and ____ systems.
e: The sulphur cycle moves through the rocks, water bodies, atmosphere and living systems. The sulphur cycle moves sulphur among rocks, water, air, and organisms.

q: Sulphur is one of the components that make up proteins and ____.
e: Sulphur is one of the components that make up proteins and vitamins. Vitamins is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When sulphur dioxide enters the atmosphere, it will react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals in the atmosphere, to produce sulphur ____.
e: When sulphur dioxide enters the atmosphere, it will react with oxygen to produce sulphur trioxide gas, or with other chemicals in the atmosphere, to produce sulphur salts. Salts is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water to produce sulphuric acid (____).
e: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water to produce sulphuric acid (H2SO4). H2SO4 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sulphuric acid may also be produced from dimethyl sulphide emitted to the atmosphere by ____ species.
e: Sulphuric acid may also be produced from dimethyl sulphide emitted to the atmosphere by plankton species. Plankton is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: All these substances will settle back onto the Earth, or react with rain and fall back onto the Earth as acid ____.
e: All these substances will settle back onto the Earth, or react with rain and fall back onto the Earth as acid deposition. Deposition is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere by animal ____ practices.
e: Carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere by animal husbandry practices. Husbandry is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, changing land use, and using limestone to make concrete transfer significant quantities of carbon into the atmosphere ____.
e: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, changing land use, and using limestone to make concrete transfer significant quantities of carbon into the atmosphere rapidly. Rapidly is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The ocean absorbs much of the carbon dioxide that is released from burning fossil fuels, lowering the ocean's pH through a process called ocean ____.
e: The ocean absorbs much of the carbon dioxide that is released from burning fossil fuels, lowering the ocean's pH through a process called ocean acidification. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and ____.
e: Ocean acidification interferes with the ability of marine organisms to build their shells and skeletons. Ocean acidification is the long-term drop in seawater pH as the ocean takes up extra CO2.

q: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus that enter the ecosystem from fertiliser runoff and from sewage cause excessive growth of ____.
e: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus that enter the ecosystem from fertiliser runoff and from sewage cause excessive growth of algae. Algae is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The subsequent death and decay of these aquatic plants deplete dissolved ____, which leads to the death of aquatic organisms.
e: The subsequent death and decay of these aquatic plants deplete dissolved oxygen, which leads to the death of aquatic organisms. Oxygen is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The burning of large quantities of fossil fuels, especially coal, releases larger amounts of hydrogen ____ gas into the atmosphere.
e: The burning of large quantities of fossil fuels, especially coal, releases larger amounts of hydrogen sulphide gas into the atmosphere. Sulphide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The extraction of metals such as copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases sulphur ____.
e: The extraction of metals such as copper, lead, and zinc from sulphur-containing ores releases sulphur dioxide. Dioxide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The clean and green environment implies the absence of pollution and a better quality of ____.
e: The clean and green environment implies the absence of pollution and a better quality of life. Life is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Green technology is an environmentally friendly technology that builds products and systems to conserve natural resources and the ____.
e: Green technology is an environmentally friendly technology that builds products and systems to conserve natural resources and the environment. Environment is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of ____ substances.
e: Green chemistry is the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances. Green chemistry designs products and processes so they make less hazardous waste.

q: A green synthesis which is used in green chemistry also helps reduce harmful gas emissions, conserve water, reduce waste and utilise less consumption of ____.
e: A green synthesis which is used in green chemistry also helps reduce harmful gas emissions, conserve water, reduce waste and utilise less consumption of energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: The 7 R's of a green environment for sustainable development are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and ____.
e: The 7 R's of a green environment for sustainable development are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Regift, and Recycle. Recycle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
